task.name: Runner Capacity Incident Remediation
task.description: Review self-hosted runner queue telemetry for one configured runner label set and surface only sustained capacity incidents in which eligible workflow jobs remain queued beyond the configured threshold across three consecutive five-minute observations, without duplicating an open incident.
task.intent: Reduce operator time spent detecting and remediating sustained self-hosted runner queue capacity incidents while avoiding transient queue spikes and incidents that are already tracked.
activationConditions: At least one workflow job eligible for the configured self-hosted runner label set exceeds the configured queue-age threshold in each of three consecutive five-minute observations.

Authoritative Actions and runner evidence shows that the queued jobs lack eligible online idle capacity rather than waiting on concurrency, environment approval, dependency, or repository policy controls.
requiredEffects: Each novel incident finding identifies the runner label set, affected queued jobs, first and latest qualifying observations, queue-age threshold, eligible online and busy runner counts, and evidence excluding non-capacity blockers.
The workflow creates or updates one repository-linked incident record with bounded remediation options and lets maintainers accept, reject, or resolve the finding.
noopConditions: Queue age does not exceed the configured threshold for three consecutive observations, or eligible idle capacity exists during any qualifying observation.
Every supported incident for the same runner label set and overlapping observation interval is already represented by an open repository-linked incident record.
successConditions: A supported incident receives accepted repository remediation evidence and eligible-job queue age remains below the configured threshold for three consecutive five-minute observations within 24 hours of assignment, or it is explicitly dismissed with accepted contrary evidence.
Transient spikes, non-capacity blockers, and overlapping already-tracked incidents create no duplicate operator attention.
uncertainties: Runner registration and job telemetry can lag, so an apparently offline or saturated runner set may recover before the third observation.
A job can match multiple runner label sets; the deduplication rule assigns one incident to the most specific configured label set and records the attribution.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel sustained runner-capacity incidents assigned to the run that either receive accepted remediation evidence and demonstrate queue recovery within 24 hours or are explicitly dismissed with accepted contrary evidence.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated sustained capacity-incident episodes it assigns for one configured self-hosted runner label set.
acceptedEvidence: A merged pull request or committed repository configuration change linked from the incident record that adjusts runner autoscaling, runner-label routing, or workflow demand for the affected label set.

A maintainer-accepted incident record linked to authoritative Actions run evidence showing eligible-job queue age below the configured threshold for three consecutive five-minute observations after remediation and before the evidence cutoff.
A closed incident record that explicitly dismisses the finding with repository-linked evidence that the queue was caused by a non-capacity blocker or an approved bounded exception.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran and owns the durable incident record.
The covered repositories whose Actions run evidence supplied the assigned queued jobs.

metric.name: recovered-supported-runner-capacity-incidents
metric.formula: supported novel runner-capacity incidents with accepted remediation or dismissal evidence and, unless dismissed, three consecutive recovered observations within 24 hours / supported novel runner-capacity incidents assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 24 hours after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel runner-capacity incident was assigned and none has accepted recovery or dismissal evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned incident set, eligible-job queue observations, runner availability observations, or required repository-linked remediation evidence cannot be read for the full maturation window.

rows.finding-summary: Label set self-hosted/linux/x64 has four eligible jobs above the 10-minute threshold across three five-minute observations, zero idle and two busy runners, with concurrency and approval blockers excluded.

Label set self-hosted/windows/x64 has three eligible jobs above the 15-minute threshold across three five-minute observations, zero idle and one busy runner, with concurrency and approval blockers excluded.

rows.outcome-summary: Maintainer accepted the scaling change and three consecutive five-minute observations showed eligible queue age below 10 minutes.
